description: OpenSAND, formerly Platine, is an open-source tool that emulates an end-to-end satellite communication system, mainly DVB-S2 and DVB-RCS2, in real time. It supports transparent and regenerative satellites, mesh and star configurations, multi-spot and multi-gateway topologies, IPv4, IPv6 and Ethernet connectivity, an adaptive physical layer with simulated channel conditions, and MF-TDMA bandwidth sharing with DAMA and SCPC, and it can be interconnected with real equipment, other IP networks or the Internet. A configuration and supervision interface provides real-time and offline monitoring on a distributed platform. It was first developed by Thales Alenia Space within EU IST projects and CNES studies; the open-source community was created by CNES and Thales Alenia Space France, and it is maintained with Viveris Technologies. Coverage: generic satellite systems, not tied to a region; performance depends on the emulation hosts. Format and access: source and Linux packages from the project website and forge; free of charge under GNU GPLv3 or LGPLv3 depending on the component. Caveats: needs several Linux machines or containers; channel models are simplified; documentation is partly in the project wiki. Simulation uses: testing applications and protocols over satellite links, capacity planning of satellite backhaul, resilience of services under degraded channels, and emergency communications. Related records: SNS3 and NetSim simulate satellite systems, and ns-3 can be combined for hybrid terrestrial-satellite studies.
